source:
For something this large, Roblox Build will do much better if you give it both a layout diagram and a strict building specification.

Here's a simple top-down layout you can copy into Build:

+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| KSG TRAINING FACILITY |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

[Parking] [Main Gate] [Security Checkpoint]

+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Reception | Waiting | Front Office | Briefing Room | Staff Offices | Server Room |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Lockers | Medical | Bathrooms | Armory | Equipment | Break Room |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Classroom | Classroom | Classroom | Simulation Room | Control Room | CCTV Room |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Indoor Shooting Range (10 Lanes) | Weapons Storage | Cleaning Area |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| CQB / Kill House | Breaching House | Hallways | Tactical Village |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Gym | Obstacle Course | Training Yard | Vehicle Training Area |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Then tell the AI to follow these building rules:

Every room must have a solid concrete floor (at least 1 stud thick).

Anchor every floor so players cannot fall through.

Every room must have four full-height walls.

Every room must have a complete roof and ceiling.

No gaps beside doors.

Doors must fit tightly inside the wall frame.

Walls must have collisions enabled.

Floors, roofs, and stairs must all have collisions enabled.

Laptops should sit on desks in the Front Office, Control Room, Staff Offices, Reception, and Briefing Room.

Add chairs, filing cabinets, lockers, CCTV monitors, desks, lights, vents, and emergency exits.

Use realistic concrete, steel, and industrial materials.

Scale the map realistically with wide hallways and large rooms.

Do not generate cartoon buildings or low-poly parts.


This should stop the issues where:

You fall through the floor.

Doors have gaps you can walk through.

Buildings have missing roofs.

Half-height walls appear.

Furniture floats or clips through the floor.


For a project like this, I'd also recommend generating one building at a time (for example, Reception, then the Shooting Range, then the CQB building) and connecting them afterward. Roblox Build is much more reliable with smaller sections than trying to generate an entire military base in one prompt.

image_prompt.text: Every room of the facility as a real enterable space - reception, offices, classrooms, armory, medical, locker rooms, control and CCTV rooms, and the indoor shooting range
Wide hallways inside each block and outdoor paths connecting the blocks, sized so the rows of rooms read as one facility
A fenced perimeter broken by the main gate and a security checkpoint at the front
A parking area in front of the main gate
An indoor shooting range with ten lanes, weapons storage, and a cleaning area
A CQB kill house and a breaching house with practice hallways
A tactical village of mock street buildings for training
An outdoor training yard with an obstacle course, a gym, and a vehicle training area
Office and support rooms furnished with desks holding laptops, chairs, filing cabinets, lockers, CCTV monitors, lights, vents, and emergency exits
Realistic concrete and steel industrial construction throughout, no cartoon or low-poly forms

layout_placement.text: Room adjacency fixed by the user's own top-down diagram - six rows of rooms behind a front strip of parking, main gate, and security checkpoint

notes: The user supplied an explicit top-down floor plan and a list of construction rules (1-stud anchored floors, four full-height walls, complete roofs, tight door frames, collisions on every surface). Nothing in the handoff can carry an authored plan, so it survives only here.
must-be-valid is on the route because the construction rules are the request - a free image will not guarantee sealed rooms or gap-free doors.
The user recommends generating one building at a time and connecting them afterward, which the single-frame route does not support.
No preset was taken: none of the three no-genre presets describes a room-program build.

answers.ask: Roughly how large should the whole compound be - a few hundred studs across, or a full military-base footprint?
answers.answer: Keep it to a few hundred studs across: a compact, realistically scaled training facility rather than a full military-base footprint.

answers.ask: Is this a playable game, a group training map, or a static build to walk around?
answers.answer: This is a group training map that players can walk around and use for organized training.
